title: R-Codes visual privacy: major openings overlooking a neighbour
edition: State Planning Policy 7.3, Residential Design Codes Volume 1
disclaimer: PLANNING, NOT BUILDING CODE, AND SIMPLIFIED GEOMETRY. The R-Codes control overlooking through a CONE OF VISION -- a 45 degree arc swung from each major opening -- not through a plain perpendicular setback. What is checked here is the perpendicular distance from the window's wall to the boundary it faces, which is the cone at its worst case: a window set back far enough perpendicular is set back far enough in every direction, but a window that fails here may still comply once the cone is drawn, because the cone can fall across a corner of the lot rather than across the neighbour. So a FAIL here is a prompt to draw the cone, not a finding that the design is non-compliant. A PASS is meaningful; a fail is a question. The setback figures must be confirmed against the current version of the table -- they are reproduced here at medium confidence and the R-Codes are amended regularly. Screening, obscure glazing above 1.6 m sill, and boundary walls all change the answer and none of them are modelled. Local Development Plans routinely override these figures for a specific estate.

rules.title: Visual privacy: bedrooms and studies
rules.applies_when: on_exterior_wall and floor_above_ground_mm > 500 and boundary_setback_mm != None and ('bedroom' in serves_functions or 'office' in serves_functions)
rules.message: A bedroom or study window {width_mm} mm wide sits {boundary_setback_mm} mm from the boundary, with its floor {floor_above_ground_mm} mm above ground. The R-Codes look for 4.5 m to a bedroom or study. Draw the cone of vision before treating this as a fail.
rules.note: Applies only where the floor is more than 0.5 m above natural ground, which is why a slab-on-ground single storey does not trigger it and a first floor does.

rules.title: Visual privacy: other habitable rooms
rules.applies_when: on_exterior_wall and floor_above_ground_mm > 500 and boundary_setback_mm != None and ('living' in serves_functions or 'dining' in serves_functions or 'kitchen' in serves_functions)
rules.message: A living, dining or kitchen window sits {boundary_setback_mm} mm from the boundary, with its floor {floor_above_ground_mm} mm above ground. The R-Codes look for 6 m to a habitable room other than a bedroom or study.
rules.note: A living room is treated more strictly than a bedroom because it is occupied for longer and at different hours.

rules.title: Visual privacy: balconies and unenclosed outdoor living
rules.message: {name} is an unenclosed outdoor living space above ground level. The R-Codes look for 7.5 m to a boundary from one -- the longest of the three setbacks, because a balcony overlooks continuously and in every direction.
rules.note: Reported whenever such a space occurs above ground, because its cone of vision sweeps the whole lot and the perpendicular distance from one wall does not describe it. This one genuinely needs the cone drawn.

rules.title: The boundary distance is known
rules.message: The distance from this window to the boundary could not be worked out, so no privacy check was made on it.
rules.note: Happens on a lot whose boundary is not orthogonal to the wall. The distance is left unknown rather than guessed, so the rule reports rather than passing in silence.
